questions.stem: A current is said to have a set of 135 degrees. What does this mean?
options: The water is coming from the south-east
The wind is blowing toward the south-east
questions.explanation: Set is the direction toward which the current flows. A wind is named by the direction it blows from, which is the usual source of confusion.

questions.stem: Which statement defines rate and drift correctly?
options: Rate is the distance carried; drift is the speed in knots
Both are directions, in degrees true
Rate: speed in knots; drift: distance carried
Rate is the direction; drift is the speed
questions.explanation: Rate (knots) multiplied by time (hours) gives drift (nautical miles). Some books use 'drift' for the speed, so check the units asked for.

questions.stem: A current sets 270 degrees at 2.5 knots. How far does it carry the ship in 45 minutes?
questions.explanation: Drift = rate x time = 2.5 x 0.75 = 1.875, about 1.9 nm toward 270 degrees. 112 forgets to divide by 60, and 3.3 divides by 0.75.

questions.stem: A fix is taken 1.5 hours after the DR was started. It lies 2.0 nm from the DR position in the direction 045 degrees. What are the set and the rate?
questions.explanation: The direction from the DR to the fix is the set. The drift of 2.0 nm over 1.5 hours is 2.0 / 1.5 = 1.3 knots. 225 reverses the direction, 2.0 knots forgets the time, and 3.0 multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.stem: Why can the difference between a DR and a fix not simply be called 'the current'?
options: It includes only the effect of wind
It is always larger than the current
It includes leeway and other errors too
It is measured in the wrong units
questions.explanation: The offset is the sum of everything the DR ignored. If the log reads high or the compass error is uncorrected, those errors appear in the offset.

questions.stem: A ship steers 000 degrees at 6 knots for 3 hours. The current sets 090 degrees at 1.0 knot. Which gives the track and speed made good?
questions.explanation: DR distance 18 nm north; drift 3.0 nm east. Track = arctan(3.0 / 18) = 9.5 degrees from north toward east, so 009 degrees. Distance = square root of (18 squared + 3 squared) = 18.2 nm in 3 hours, 6.1 knots. 081 uses the wrong ratio, 351 the wrong side, and 7.0 adds the rate.

questions.stem: How is the estimated position found from a DR and a known set and rate?
options: From the DR, along the set, for rate x time
Draw the set direction from the last fix for the distance of the DR
Draw the reciprocal of the set from the DR
Move the DR by the rate in the direction of the track
questions.explanation: The current carries the ship from where the DR places her, in the direction of its set, by the drift in the time since the last fix. The end of that line is the EP.

questions.stem: A current sets 270 degrees. In which direction does it push the ship?
questions.explanation: Set is the direction toward which the current flows. 270 degrees is west.

questions.stem: After finding the set and drift from a DR and a fix, from where is the next DR laid?
questions.explanation: A fix restarts the dead reckoning. The offset is carried forward as a set and drift if the current is expected to persist.
